```python
from manim import *
class AnimateSyntax(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        s = Square(color=GREEN, fill_opacity=0.5)
        c = Circle(color=RED, fill_opacity=0.5)
        self.add(s, c)
        self.play(s.animate.shift(UP), c.animate.shift(DOWN))
        self.play(VGroup(s, c).animate.arrange(RIGHT))
        self.play(c.animate(rate_func=linear).shift(RIGHT).scale(2))
        self.wait()
```

```python
from manim import *
import numpy as np
from forge.beats import ForgeScene, beat


class CrossProductArea(ForgeScene):
    origin = np.array([-4.5, -1.5, 0.0])
    vec_a = np.array([3.2, 0.0, 0.0])
    vec_b = np.array([1.4, 2.6, 0.0])

    @beat("Introduce vectors a and b", seconds=4)
    def introduce_vectors(self):
        self.arrow_a = Arrow(
            self.origin, self.origin + self.vec_a, buff=0, color=BLUE_C
        )
        self.arrow_b = Arrow(
            self.origin, self.origin + self.vec_b, buff=0, color=YELLOW_C
        )

        self.label_a = MathTex(r"\vec{a}", color=BLUE_C).next_to(
            self.arrow_a, DOWN, buff=0.15
        )
        self.label_b = MathTex(r"\vec{b}", color=YELLOW_C).next_to(
            self.arrow_b.get_center(), UL, buff=0.15
        )

        self.play(
            GrowArrow(self.arrow_a),
            Write(self.label_a),
            GrowArrow(self.arrow_b),
            Write(self.label_b),
            run_time=2.5,
        )
        self.wait(1.5)

    @beat("Construct the spanned parallelogram", seconds=4)
    def construct_parallelogram(self):
        p0 = self.origin
        p1 = self.origin + self.vec_a
        p2 = self.origin + self.vec_a + self.vec_b
        p3 = self.origin + self.vec_b

        self.parallelogram = Polygon(
            p0, p1, p2, p3,
            fill_color=TEAL_E,
            fill_opacity=0.45,
            stroke_color=TEAL_B,
            stroke_width=2,
        )

        edge_top = DashedLine(p3, p2, color=BLUE_C)
        edge_right = DashedLine(p1, p2, color=YELLOW_C)

        self.play(
            Create(edge_top),
            Create(edge_right),
            FadeIn(self.parallelogram),
            run_time=2.5,
        )
        self.wait(1.5)

    @beat("Deconstruct geometric height and angle", seconds=4)
    def show_height_and_angle(self):
        p_drop = np.array([self.origin[0] + self.vec_b[0], self.origin[1], 0.0])
        p_top = self.origin + self.vec_b

        self.height_line = DashedLine(p_top, p_drop, color=RED_C, stroke_width=3)
        self.height_label = MathTex(
            r"h = \|\vec{b}\|\sin\theta", font_size=28, color=RED_C
        ).next_to(self.height_line, LEFT, buff=0.1)

        line_a = Line(self.origin, self.origin + self.vec_a)
        line_b = Line(self.origin, self.origin + self.vec_b)
        self.angle_arc = Angle(line_a, line_b, radius=0.65, color=WHITE)
        self.theta_label = MathTex(r"\theta", font_size=26).next_to(
            self.angle_arc, UR, buff=0.05
        )

        self.play(
            Create(self.angle_arc),
            Write(self.theta_label),
            Create(self.height_line),
            Write(self.height_label),
            run_time=2.5,
        )
        self.wait(1.5)

    @beat("Derive the cross product magnitude formula", seconds=4)
    def derive_formula(self):
        title = Text("Parallelogram Area", font_size=32, color=WHITE).move_to(
            [3.2, 2.2, 0]
        )
        eq1 = MathTex(r"\text{Area} = \text{base} \times \text{height}", font_size=30)
        eq2 = MathTex(r"= \|\vec{a}\| \cdot (\|\vec{b}\|\sin\theta)", font_size=30)
        eq3 = MathTex(r"= \|\vec{a} \times \vec{b}\|", font_size=34, color=YELLOW_C)

        formula_group = (
            VGroup(title, eq1, eq2, eq3)
            .arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.35)
            .move_to([3.2, 0.8, 0])
        )

        self.play(Write(title), run_time=0.8)
        self.play(Write(eq1), run_time=1.0)
        self.play(Write(eq2), run_time=1.0)
        self.play(Write(eq3), run_time=1.0)
        self.formula_group = formula_group

    @beat("Compute the numerical area dynamically", seconds=4)
    def compute_numerical_area(self):
        # Compute exact values programmatically from vector coordinates
        cross_vector = np.cross(self.vec_a, self.vec_b)
        area_val = np.linalg.norm(cross_vector)
        norm_a_val = np.linalg.norm(self.vec_a)
        norm_b_val = np.linalg.norm(self.vec_b)

        calc_box = RoundedRectangle(
            corner_radius=0.15,
            width=4.6,
            height=1.8,
            color=GRAY_B,
            fill_color=DARK_GRAY,
            fill_opacity=0.3,
        ).move_to([3.2, -2.0, 0])

        calc_label = VGroup(
            MathTex(
                rf"\|\vec{{a}}\| = {norm_a_val:.1f},\quad \|\vec{{b}}\| \approx {norm_b_val:.2f}",
                font_size=24,
            ),
            MathTex(
                rf"\text{{Computed Area}} = {area_val:.2f}",
                font_size=30,
                color=GREEN_C,
            ),
        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.25).move_to(calc_box)

        self.play(
            Create(calc_box),
            Write(calc_label),
            self.parallelogram.animate.set_fill(GREEN_D, opacity=0.55),
            run_time=2.5,
        )
        self.wait(1.5)
```

Exploring Symmetries with Semidirect Products In what ways can a semidirect product be used to model symmetries of a 3-dimensional object?

```python
from manim import *

class SemidirectProductSymmetries(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # Title
        title = Text("Exploring Symmetries with Semidirect Products", color=WHITE).scale(0.7)
        self.play(Write(title))
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(title.animate.to_edge(UP))
        
        # Introduction: Symmetries in 3D objects
        intro_text = Text("Symmetries in 3D objects", color=WHITE).scale(0.6)
        self.play(Write(intro_text))
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(FadeOut(intro_text))
        
        # Key Concept 1: Rotations (Group G)
        sphere = Circle(radius=1.5, color=BLUE)
        self.play(Create(sphere))
        
        rotation_arrow = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=UP, color=YELLOW)
        self.play(Create(rotation_arrow))
        
        rotation_text = Text("Rotations (Group G)", color=YELLOW).scale(0.6).next_to(sphere, DOWN)
        self.play(Write(rotation_text))
        self.play(Rotate(rotation_arrow, angle=PI, about_point=ORIGIN))
        
        # Key Concept 2: Reflections (Group H)
        reflection_line = Line(start=sphere.get_center() + LEFT*2, end=sphere.get_center() + RIGHT*2, color=RED)
        self.play(Create(reflection_line))
        
        reflection_text = Text("Reflections (Group H)", color=RED).scale(0.6).next_to(rotation_text, DOWN)
        self.play(Write(reflection_text))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Clean up visual elements
        self.play(FadeOut(rotation_arrow, reflection_line))
        
        # Key Concept 3: Semidirect Product
        semidirect_text = Text("G ⋊ H", color=WHITE).scale(0.8)
        self.play(Write(semidirect_text))
        self.play(semidirect_text.animate.to_corner(UL).shift(RIGHT+DOWN))
        
        # Add the operation equation
        operation_text = Text("gh = g·φ(h)", color=WHITE).scale(0.7)
        self.play(Write(operation_text))
        self.play(operation_text.animate.next_to(semidirect_text, DOWN).align_to(semidirect_text, LEFT))
        
        explanation_text = Text("Where φ represents how G acts on H", color=WHITE).scale(0.5)
        self.play(Write(explanation_text))
        self.play(explanation_text.animate.next_to(operation_text, DOWN).align_to(operation_text, LEFT))
        
        # Key Insight: Polyhedra symmetries
        cube = Square(side_length=1.5, color=GREEN).shift(RIGHT*3)  # Representing a cube with a square for simplicity
        self.play(Create(cube))
        
        insight_text = Text("3D Object Symmetries", color=GREEN).scale(0.6).next_to(cube, DOWN)
        self.play(Write(insight_text))
        
        # Show rotation symmetry
        self.play(Rotate(cube, angle=PI/2, about_point=cube.get_center()))
        self.wait(0.3)
        
        # Show reflection symmetry (by scaling negatively in x-direction)
        self.play(cube.animate.scale([-1, 1, 1]))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Clean up for conclusion
        self.play(FadeOut(sphere, rotation_text, reflection_text, semidirect_text, 
                          operation_text, explanation_text, cube, insight_text))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Conclusion
        conclusion_text = Text("Semidirect products model symmetries", color=WHITE).scale(0.7)
        self.play(Write(conclusion_text))
        
        final_text = Text("by combining rotations and reflections", color=YELLOW).scale(0.6)
        self.play(Write(final_text.next_to(conclusion_text, DOWN)))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Fade out everything
        self.play(FadeOut(title, conclusion_text, final_text))
        self.wait(0.5)
```

Converging Bets: Martingale Strategies Revealed How can Doob's martingale convergence theorem be applied to prove the convergence of betting strategies?

```python
from manim import *

class MartingaleConvergence(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # Title
        title = Text("Converging Bets: Martingale Strategies Revealed", color=BLUE).scale(0.7)
        self.play(Write(title))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(title.animate.shift(UP*2))  # More compatible than to_edge
        
        # Introduction - Casino setting
        casino_text = Text("Imagine you're at a casino...", color=WHITE).scale(0.6)
        self.play(Write(casino_text))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(casino_text))
        
        # Key Concept 1 - Doubling strategy
        strategy_text = Text("The Doubling Strategy", color=RED).scale(0.7)
        self.play(Write(strategy_text))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Simple animation of betting chips
        chip = Circle(radius=0.2, color=GREEN, fill_opacity=1).move_to(LEFT*2)
        lose_text = Text("Lose", color=RED).scale(0.5).next_to(chip, DOWN)
        
        self.play(Create(chip))
        self.play(Write(lose_text))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Double the bet
        doubled_chip1 = Circle(radius=0.2, color=GREEN, fill_opacity=1).move_to(RIGHT*0.5)
        doubled_chip2 = Circle(radius=0.2, color=GREEN, fill_opacity=1).move_to(RIGHT*1)
        double_text = Text("Double", color=YELLOW).scale(0.5).next_to(doubled_chip1, DOWN)
        
        self.play(Create(doubled_chip1), Create(doubled_chip2))
        self.play(Write(double_text))
        self.wait(1)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(strategy_text), FadeOut(chip), FadeOut(lose_text), 
                 FadeOut(doubled_chip1), FadeOut(doubled_chip2), FadeOut(double_text))
        
        # Key Concept 2 - Martingale definition
        martingale_title = Text("What is a Martingale?", color=BLUE).scale(0.7)
        self.play(Write(martingale_title))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Simplified martingale equation (using Text instead of MathTex for better compatibility)
        martingale_eq = Text("E[X_{n+1} | X_1, X_2, ..., X_n] = X_n", color=WHITE).scale(0.7)
        self.play(Write(martingale_eq))
        self.wait(1)
        
        fair_game_text = Text("A fair game with no memory", color=WHITE).scale(0.5).next_to(martingale_eq, DOWN)
        self.play(Write(fair_game_text))
        self.wait(1)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(martingale_title), FadeOut(martingale_eq), FadeOut(fair_game_text))
        
        # Key Concept 3 - Doob's theorem
        doob_title = Text("Doob's Martingale Convergence Theorem", color=YELLOW).scale(0.6)
        self.play(Write(doob_title))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Simplified graph - just an arrow for x-axis
        x_axis = Arrow(start=LEFT*3, end=RIGHT*3, color=WHITE)
        time_label = Text("Time", color=WHITE).scale(0.4).next_to(x_axis, DOWN)
        self.play(Create(x_axis), Write(time_label))
        
        # Plot dots to show fluctuation and convergence
        dots = []
        positions = [
            LEFT*3 + UP*1,    # Start high
            LEFT*2 + DOWN*0.5, # Drop down
            LEFT*1 + UP*0.8,   # Back up
            ORIGIN + DOWN*0.3, # Down again
            RIGHT*1 + UP*0.2,  # Slight up
            RIGHT*2 + DOWN*0.1, # Slight down
            RIGHT*3,           # Converge to 0
        ]
        
        for pos in positions:
            dot = Dot(point=pos, color=RED)
            dots.append(dot)
            self.play(Create(dot))
        
        # Connect dots with lines to show path
        for i in range(len(dots)-1):
            line = Line(dots[i].get_center(), dots[i+1].get_center(), color=RED)
            self.play(Create(line))
        
        # Convergence line
        conv_line = DashedLine(start=LEFT*3, end=RIGHT*3, color=GREEN)
        conv_text = Text("Convergence", color=GREEN).scale(0.4).next_to(conv_line, UP)
        self.play(Create(conv_line), Write(conv_text))
        
        # Simplified convergence equation
        conv_eq = Text("lim(n→∞) X_n = X", color=WHITE).scale(0.6)
        self.play(Write(conv_eq.shift(DOWN*2)))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Clean up the graph elements
        self.play(
            *[FadeOut(obj) for obj in [doob_title, x_axis, time_label, conv_line, conv_text, conv_eq] + dots]
        )
        
        # Key Insight
        insight_text = Text("Martingale strategies converge but\ncan't overcome house edge", color=WHITE).scale(0.6)
        self.play(Write(insight_text))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(insight_text))
        
        # Conclusion
        conclusion = Text("Doob's theorem offers mathematical boundaries\nto betting strategies", color=BLUE).scale(0.6)
        self.play(Write(conclusion))
        self.wait(1)
        
        final_text = Text("Happy learning!", color=GREEN).scale(0.5).next_to(conclusion, DOWN)
        self.play(Write(final_text))
        self.wait(2)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(conclusion), FadeOut(final_text), FadeOut(title))
```

Exploring Equilibrium: A Journey into Discount Factors and Repeated Games How does one model the emergence of a subgame-perfect Nash equilibrium in infinitely repeated games when different discount factors are assigned to players?

```python
from manim import *

class GameTheoryDiscountFactors(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # Title
        title = Text("Exploring Equilibrium in Repeated Games", font_size=32)
        self.play(Write(title))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(title))
        
        # Element 1: Decision tree for repeated games
        tree_title = Text("Decision Tree in Repeated Games", font_size=28)
        self.play(Write(tree_title))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(tree_title.animate.to_edge(UP))
        
        # Simple tree with two branches
        root = Dot()
        branch1 = Arrow(root.get_center(), UP + RIGHT)
        branch2 = Arrow(root.get_center(), UP - RIGHT)
        
        self.play(Create(root))
        self.play(Create(branch1), Create(branch2))
        
        label1 = Text("Cooperate", font_size=20).next_to(branch1.get_end(), RIGHT)
        label2 = Text("Defect", font_size=20).next_to(branch2.get_end(), LEFT)
        
        self.play(Write(label1), Write(label2))
        self.wait(1)
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(tree_title), FadeOut(root), FadeOut(branch1), 
            FadeOut(branch2), FadeOut(label1), FadeOut(label2)
        )
        
        # Element 2: Players with different discount factors
        player_title = Text("Players with Different Discount Factors", font_size=28)
        self.play(Write(player_title))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(player_title.animate.to_edge(UP))
        
        player1 = Circle(radius=0.5, color=BLUE).shift(LEFT * 2)
        player2 = Circle(radius=0.5, color=RED).shift(RIGHT * 2)
        
        delta1 = MathTex(r"\delta_1 = 0.9", font_size=24).next_to(player1, DOWN)
        delta2 = MathTex(r"\delta_2 = 0.6", font_size=24).next_to(player2, DOWN)
        
        self.play(Create(player1), Create(player2))
        self.play(Write(delta1), Write(delta2))
        
        patience = Text("Patient vs. Impatient", font_size=24).to_edge(DOWN)
        self.play(Write(patience))
        
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(
            FadeOut(player_title), FadeOut(player1), FadeOut(player2),
            FadeOut(delta1), FadeOut(delta2), FadeOut(patience)
        )
```

```python
class DualSpacesScene(Scene):

        # Title
        title = Text("Navigating Dual Spaces", font_size=36)
        subtitle = Text("A Journey through Bases", font_size=24).next_to(title, DOWN)
        
        self.play(Write(title))
        self.play(Write(subtitle))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(title), FadeOut(subtitle))
        
        # Vector space - left side
        v_axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            axis_config={"color": BLUE},
        ).scale(0.8).shift(LEFT*3)
        
        # Original square basis
        v1 = Arrow(start=v_axes.get_origin(), end=v_axes.c2p(1, 0), color=GREEN, buff=0)
        v2 = Arrow(start=v_axes.get_origin(), end=v_axes.c2p(0, 1), color=RED, buff=0)
        
        v1_label = Text("v₁", font_size=20, color=GREEN).next_to(v1, DOWN)
        v2_label = Text("v₂", font_size=20, color=RED).next_to(v2, LEFT)
        
        vector_space_title = Text("Vector Space", font_size=24, color=BLUE).next_to(v_axes, UP)
        
        # Vector space equation
        v_eq = MathTex("V = \\text{span}(\\{v_1, v_2\\})").scale(0.7).next_to(v_axes, DOWN)
        
        # Create vector space
        self.play(Create(v_axes), Write(vector_space_title))
        self.play(Create(v1), Create(v2))
        self.play(Write(v1_label), Write(v2_label))
        self.play(Write(v_eq))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Dual space - right side
        d_axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            axis_config={"color": ORANGE},
        ).scale(0.8).shift(RIGHT*3)
        
        # Dual basis (represented as dashed lines)
        f1 = DashedLine(start=d_axes.get_origin(), end=d_axes.c2p(1, 0), color=YELLOW)
        f2 = DashedLine(start=d_axes.get_origin(), end=d_axes.c2p(0, 1), color=GOLD)
        
        f1_label = Text("f₁", font_size=20, color=YELLOW).next_to(f1, DOWN)

        dual_space_title = Text("Dual Space", font_size=24, color=ORANGE).next_to(d_axes, UP)
        
        # Dual space equation
        d_eq = MathTex("V^* = \\text{span}(\\{f_1, f_2\\})").scale(0.7).next_to(d_axes, DOWN)
        
        # Create dual space
        self.play(Create(d_axes), Write(dual_space_title))
        self.play(Create(f1), Create(f2))
        self.play(Write(f1_label), Write(f2_label))
        self.play(Write(d_eq))
        self.wait(1)

        change_text = Text("Changing the basis...", font_size=28).to_edge(UP)
        self.play(Write(change_text))

        new_v1_label = Text("v₁", font_size=20, color=GREEN).next_to(new_v1, UP+RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        new_v2_label = Text("v₂", font_size=20, color=RED).next_to(new_v2, DOWN+RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        # Transform vector space basis

        new_f2 = DashedLine(start=d_axes.get_origin(), end=d_axes.c2p(0.7, -0.7), color=GOLD)
        
        new_f1_label = Text("f₁", font_size=20, color=YELLOW).next_to(new_f1, UP+RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        new_f2_label = Text("f₂", font_size=20, color=GOLD).next_to(new_f2, DOWN+RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(
            Transform(f1, new_f1),
            Transform(f2, new_f2),
            Transform(f1_label, new_f1_label),
            Transform(f2_label, new_f2_label)
        )
        
        self.play(FadeOut(change_text))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Matrix representation

        self.play(FadeOut(matrix_text), FadeOut(matrix_eq))

        # Final cleanup
```

Display a filled triangle at the center of the screen and a square positioned on the left edge. As the animation begins, the triangle continuously spins around the center of the screen, while the square smoothly moves from the left edge to the right edge. The triangle keeps rotating throughout the square’s movement. This gives an illusion that the triangle is moving to the left while in actuality it is the square at the back moving to the right.

```python
from manim import *

class SpinningTriangle(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        tri = Triangle().set_fill(opacity=1).set_z_index(2)
        sq = Square().to_edge(LEFT)

        # will keep spinning while there is an animation going on
        always_rotate(tri, rate=2*PI, about_point=ORIGIN)

        self.add(tri, sq)
        self.play(sq.animate.to_edge(RIGHT), rate_func=linear, run_time=1)
```

```python
        phase_circle = Circle(radius=2, color=BLUE)

        self.play(FadeIn(intro_text), run_time=1)
```

```python
from manim import *

class ResidueTheoremScene(Scene):

        # Title
        title = Text("The Dance of Poles: Understanding the Residue Theorem", font_size=28)
        self.play(Write(title))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(title))
        
        # Create a simple coordinate system
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            y_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            x_length=6,
            y_length=6,
        )
        
        x_label = Text("Re(z)", font_size=20).next_to(axes.x_axis, RIGHT)
        y_label = Text("Im(z)", font_size=20).next_to(axes.y_axis, UP)
        
        self.play(Create(axes), Write(x_label), Write(y_label))
        
        # Add poles
        pole1 = Dot(axes.c2p(1, 1), color=RED)
        pole2 = Dot(axes.c2p(-1, 0.5), color=RED)
        pole3 = Dot(axes.c2p(0.5, -1), color=RED)
        poles = VGroup(pole1, pole2, pole3)
        
        # Simple pole labels
        pole_labels = VGroup(
            Text("Pole", font_size=18).next_to(pole1, UR, buff=0.1),
            Text("Pole", font_size=18).next_to(pole2, UL, buff=0.1),
            Text("Pole", font_size=18).next_to(pole3, DR, buff=0.1)
        )
        
        self.play(Create(poles), Write(pole_labels))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Introduction text
        intro = Text("Contour integrals encircle poles in the complex plane", font_size=24)
        self.play(Write(intro.to_edge(UP)))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(intro))
        
        # Clockwise contour
        contour = Circle(radius=2.5, color=BLUE).move_to(axes.c2p(0, 0))

        self.play(Create(arrow))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Residue values for clockwise
        residue1 = Text("+1", font_size=18, color=BLUE).next_to(pole1, RIGHT)
        residue2 = Text("+1", font_size=18, color=BLUE).next_to(pole2, RIGHT)
        residue3 = Text("+1", font_size=18, color=BLUE).next_to(pole3, RIGHT)
        residues = VGroup(residue1, residue2, residue3)
        
        self.play(Write(residues))
        
        # Show equation
        eq = Text("∮ f(z)dz = -2πi × sum of residues", font_size=24).to_edge(DOWN)
        self.play(Write(eq))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Direction change
        self.play(FadeOut(direction_text))
        question = Text("What if we reverse the direction?", font_size=24)
        self.play(Write(question.to_edge(UP)))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(question))
        
        # Counterclockwise
        ccw_contour = Circle(radius=2.5, color=RED).move_to(axes.c2p(0, 0))
        ccw_text = Text("Counterclockwise Direction", font_size=24, color=RED).to_edge(UP)
        ccw_arrow = Arrow(axes.c2p(2.5, 0), axes.c2p(2.3, 0.5), color=RED, buff=0)
        
        self.play(
            Transform(contour, ccw_contour),
            Write(ccw_text)
        )
        self.play(Transform(arrow, ccw_arrow))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Updated residues
```

show how Riemann sums converge to the area under a curve — start with a couple of rectangles, keep doubling them, and show the total approaching the exact integral, then show that sampling the midpoint converges much faster

```python
"""Gold scene 005 — Riemann sums converging to an integral.

Every rectangle drawn comes from ``forge.primitives.calculus``, every total is
summed from those rectangles, and the target is a reference integral computed
independently by fine midpoint summation. The scene can therefore show the
error shrinking honestly — and would show it failing to shrink if the maths
were wrong.

The chosen cubic integrates to exactly 8 over [0, 4], which gives the
convergence a clean target rather than a number that merely looks converged.

The contrast at the end is real rather than rhetorical: left-rule error halves
each time n doubles, midpoint error falls by four. Those rates are printed by
the primitive and are what the scene animates.
"""

from manim import *

from forge.beats import ForgeScene, beat
from forge.primitives.calculus import RiemannSum, exact_integral

CURVE_C = BLUE_C
RECT_C = "#F0AC5F"
MID_C = "#5CD0B3"
DIM = GREY_B

A, B = 0.0, 4.0
PANEL_X = 3.9


def f(x: float) -> float:
    return 0.25 * x ** 3 - 1.2 * x ** 2 + 1.4 * x + 1.6


class RiemannConvergence(ForgeScene):

    exact = exact_integral(f, A, B)

    def build_axes(self) -> Axes:
        return Axes(
            x_range=[0, 4.4, 1], y_range=[0, 3.2, 1],
            x_length=6.4, y_length=4.4,
            axis_config={"include_tip": False, "stroke_width": 2,
                         "color": GREY_B, "font_size": 18},
        ).to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.75).shift(DOWN * 0.3)

    def bars(self, n: int, rule: str, color) -> VGroup:
        """Rectangles straight from the primitive — positions and heights are
        the ones the sum actually uses."""
        rs = RiemannSum(f, A, B, n, rule)
        g = VGroup()
        for r in rs.rectangles():
            if r.height <= 0:
                continue
            bl = self.axes.c2p(r.x_left, 0)
            tr = self.axes.c2p(r.x_right, r.height)
            g.add(Rectangle(width=tr[0] - bl[0], height=tr[1] - bl[1],
                            stroke_color=color, stroke_width=1.4,
                            fill_color=color, fill_opacity=0.35)
                  .move_to((bl + tr) / 2))
        return g

    def readout(self, n: int, total: float, err: float, color) -> VGroup:
        return VGroup(
            VGroup(Text("n =", font_size=24, color=DIM),
                   Text(str(n), font_size=34, color=color)
                   ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.22, aligned_edge=DOWN),
            MathTex(rf"\approx {total:.3f}", font_size=40, color=color),
            Text(f"off by {err:.3f}", font_size=22, color=DIM),
        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.22).move_to([PANEL_X, 0.9, 0])

    # -- beats ---------------------------------------------------------------

    @beat("Draw the curve and shade the area we want", seconds=14,
          narration="Here is a curve, and the area beneath it between zero and "
                    "four. That area is a single number — but there is no "
                    "obvious way to measure it, because the top edge keeps "
                    "curving.")
    def setup(self):
        self.axes = self.build_axes()
        self.curve = self.axes.plot(f, x_range=[A, B], color=CURVE_C, stroke_width=4)
        self.area = self.axes.get_area(self.curve, x_range=(A, B),
                                       color=CURVE_C, opacity=0.18)
        self.title = Text("Area under a curve", font_size=30).to_edge(UP, buff=0.35)

        self.play(FadeIn(self.title, shift=DOWN * 0.2), Create(self.axes), run_time=1.2)
        self.play(Create(self.curve), run_time=1.6)
        self.play(FadeIn(self.area), run_time=1.1)
        self.wait(0.6)

    @beat("Approximate it crudely with two rectangles", seconds=14,
          narration="So approximate it with something we can measure. Two "
                    "rectangles, each as tall as the curve at its left edge. "
                    "It is clearly too small — every rectangle falls short "
                    "where the curve rises above it.")
    def crude(self):
        n = 2
        rs = RiemannSum(f, A, B, n, "left")
        self.rects = self.bars(n, "left", RECT_C)
        self.panel = self.readout(n, rs.total, abs(rs.total - self.exact), RECT_C)

        self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(r, scale=0.8) for r in self.rects],
                              lag_ratio=0.2, run_time=1.4))
        self.play(FadeIn(self.panel, shift=UP * 0.15), run_time=0.9)
        self.wait(1.2)

    @beat("Double the count and watch the gap close", seconds=12,
          narration="Now use more, thinner rectangles. Four. Eight. Sixteen. "
                    "Thirty-two. Each time the count doubles, the gap left "
                    "over is cut roughly in half — and the total climbs "
                    "steadily toward something.")
    def refine(self):
        for n in (4, 8, 16, 32):
            rs = RiemannSum(f, A, B, n, "left")
            fresh = self.bars(n, "left", RECT_C)
            panel = self.readout(n, rs.total, abs(rs.total - self.exact), RECT_C)
            # Fade rather than Transform: morphing one group of rectangles into
            # a differently-sized group pairs them arbitrarily and smears.
            self.play(FadeOut(self.rects, run_time=0.35))
            self.rects = fresh
            self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(r) for r in self.rects],
                                  lag_ratio=0.02, run_time=0.8),
                      ReplacementTransform(self.panel, panel))
            self.panel = panel
            self.wait(0.5)
        self.wait(0.6)

    @beat("Name the limit it is climbing towards", seconds=12,
          narration="That something is the integral: the exact area, equal to "
                    "eight. The rectangles never reach it with any finite "
                    "count — but they get as close as you care to ask.")
    def limit(self):
        target = VGroup(
            MathTex(r"\int_0^4 f(x)\,dx", font_size=44, color=CURVE_C),
            MathTex(rf"= {self.exact:.0f}", font_size=48, color=CURVE_C),
        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.28).move_to([PANEL_X, -1.5, 0])

        self.play(Write(target[0]), run_time=1.2)
        self.play(Write(target[1]), run_time=0.9)
        self.play(Indicate(target[1], color=CURVE_C, scale_factor=1.15), run_time=0.9)
        self.target = target
        self.wait(1.0)

    @beat("Sampling the middle instead converges far faster", seconds=20,
          narration="One change makes this dramatically better. Take each "
                    "rectangle's height from the middle of its interval rather "
                    "than the left edge. The overshoot on one side now cancels "
                    "the undershoot on the other — and with just eight "
                    "rectangles the error is smaller than the left rule "
                    "manages with sixty-four.")
    def midpoint(self):
        n = 8
        left = RiemannSum(f, A, B, n, "left")
        mid = RiemannSum(f, A, B, n, "midpoint")
        far_left = RiemannSum(f, A, B, 64, "left")
        # The scene's claim, asserted rather than trusted.
        assert abs(mid.total - self.exact) < abs(far_left.total - self.exact)

        fresh = self.bars(n, "midpoint", MID_C)
        self.play(FadeOut(self.rects, run_time=0.4))
        self.rects = fresh
        self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(r, scale=0.85) for r in self.rects],
                              lag_ratio=0.06, run_time=1.3))

        compare = VGroup(
            Text(f"left, n=8      off by {abs(left.total-self.exact):.3f}",
                 font_size=21, color=RECT_C),
            Text(f"left, n=64     off by {abs(far_left.total-self.exact):.3f}",
                 font_size=21, color=RECT_C),
            Text(f"midpoint, n=8  off by {abs(mid.total-self.exact):.3f}",
                 font_size=21, color=MID_C),
        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.2, aligned_edge=LEFT).move_to([PANEL_X, 0.9, 0])
```

```python
from manim import *

class FanoVarietiesScene(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # Introduction with title
        title = Text("Fano Varieties: Unveiling Curvature and Minimal Models", font_size=28)
        self.play(Write(title))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(title))
        
        # Create a landscape-style "Fano variety" using a polygon
        # The peaks and valleys represent the complex structure of a Fano variety
        fano_points = [
            [-4, -1, 0], [-3, 0, 0], [-2, -2, 0], [-1, 1, 0], 
            [0, -1, 0], [1, 2, 0], [2, 0, 0], [3, -1, 0], [4, 0, 0],
            [4, -2, 0], [-4, -2, 0]  # Bottom points to close the shape
        ]
        fano_variety = Polygon(*fano_points, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5)
        
        self.play(Create(fano_variety))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Add a grid representing the anticanonical bundle
        # This translucent grid symbolizes the mathematical structure guiding contractions
        grid = VGroup()
        for x in np.arange(-4, 5, 1):
            grid.add(Line(start=[x, -2, 0], end=[x, 2, 0], stroke_opacity=0.3))
        for y in np.arange(-2, 3, 1):
            grid.add(Line(start=[-4, y, 0], end=[4, y, 0], stroke_opacity=0.3))
        
        self.play(Create(grid))
        
        # Highlight curves on the variety that will contract
        curve1 = Line(start=[-2, -2, 0], end=[-1, 1, 0], stroke_width=6, color=RED)
        curve2 = Line(start=[0, -1, 0], end=[1, 2, 0], stroke_width=6, color=RED)
        
        self.play(Create(curve1), Create(curve2))
        
        # Display the anticanonical bundle equation
        eq1 = Text("-K_X > 0", font_size=24).to_edge(UP)
        self.play(Write(eq1))
        
        # Contract the curves (visualizing the birational transformation)
        contracted_curve1 = Line(start=[-1.5, -0.5, 0], end=[-1.5, -0.5, 0], stroke_width=6, color=RED)
        contracted_curve2 = Line(start=[0.5, 0.5, 0], end=[0.5, 0.5, 0], stroke_width=6, color=RED)
        
        self.play(
            Transform(curve1, contracted_curve1),
            Transform(curve2, contracted_curve2)
        )
        
        # Create a minimal model (simpler shape)
        # This represents the end result of contracting curves guided by the anticanonical bundle
        minimal_points = [
            [-4, -1, 0], [-2, -0.5, 0], [0, 0, 0], [2, 0.5, 0], [4, 0, 0],
            [4, -2, 0], [-4, -2, 0]  # Bottom points to close the shape
        ]
        minimal_model = Polygon(*minimal_points, color=GREEN, fill_opacity=0.5)
        
        # Transform the original variety to the minimal model
        self.play(Transform(fano_variety, minimal_model))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Clear the screen for the final comparison
        self.play(
            FadeOut(grid),
            FadeOut(curve1),
            FadeOut(curve2),
            FadeOut(eq1),
            FadeOut(fano_variety)
        )
        
        # Show the original and minimal model side by side for comparison
        original_model = Polygon(*fano_points, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5)
        final_minimal_model = Polygon(*minimal_points, color=GREEN, fill_opacity=0.5)
        
        # Position them on opposite sides of the screen
        original_model.scale(0.5).shift(LEFT * 3)
        final_minimal_model.scale(0.5).shift(RIGHT * 3)
        
        self.play(
            Create(original_model),
            Create(final_minimal_model)
        )
        
        # Add labels to clarify the comparison
        original_label = Text("Original Fano Variety", font_size=20).next_to(original_model, DOWN)
        minimal_label = Text("Minimal Model", font_size=20).next_to(final_minimal_model, DOWN)

            Write(original_label),
            Write(minimal_label)

        # Final message summarizing the key insight
        final_text = Text("From Complexity to Simplicity", font_size=28).to_edge(UP)
```

```python
        score_value = Text(f"{accuracy_pct}% ({correct_count}/{len(self.test_group)})", font_size=32, color=YELLOW_C).move_to(score_box.get_center() + DOWN * 0.2)
        
        self.play(
```

```python
from manim import *

class NegativeFrequenciesScene(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # Title
        title = Text("The Harmony of Frequencies", font_size=40)
        subtitle = Text("Unveiling Negative Frequencies", font_size=32)
        subtitle.next_to(title, DOWN)
        
        self.play(Write(title))
        self.play(Write(subtitle))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(title), FadeOut(subtitle))
        
        # Time domain signal
        time_text = Text("Real signal in time domain", font_size=32)
        time_text.to_edge(UP)
        
        # Simple sine wave
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-5, 5, 1],
            y_range=[-1.5, 1.5, 0.5],
        )
        
        # Creating a sine wave
        sine_graph = axes.plot(lambda x: np.sin(2 * x), color=BLUE)
        
        self.play(Write(time_text))
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(sine_graph))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Fourier Transform equation
        fourier_text = Text("Fourier Transform:", font_size=28)
        fourier_text.next_to(axes, DOWN, buff=0.2)
        
        fourier_eq = MathTex(r"X(f) = \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} x(t) e^{-i 2\pi f t} \, dt")
        fourier_eq.next_to(fourier_text, DOWN, buff=0.2)
        
        self.play(Write(fourier_text))
        self.play(Write(fourier_eq))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Transform to frequency domain
        self.play(
            FadeOut(time_text),
            FadeOut(sine_graph),
            FadeOut(fourier_text),
            FadeOut(fourier_eq)
        )
        
        freq_text = Text("Frequency domain representation", font_size=32)
        freq_text.to_edge(UP)
        
        self.play(Write(freq_text))
        
        # Frequency domain representation (two spikes)
        pos_x = 2
        neg_x = -2
        height = 1
        
        pos_freq = Line(
            start=axes.c2p(pos_x, 0), 
            end=axes.c2p(pos_x, height), 
            color=RED
        )
        
        neg_freq = Line(
            start=axes.c2p(neg_x, 0), 
            end=axes.c2p(neg_x, height), 
            color=GREEN
        )
        
        pos_label = Text("+f", font_size=24, color=RED)
        pos_label.next_to(pos_freq, UP)
        
        neg_label = Text("-f", font_size=24, color=GREEN)
        neg_label.next_to(neg_freq, UP)
        
        self.play(Create(pos_freq), Write(pos_label))
        self.play(Create(neg_freq), Write(neg_label))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Symmetry text and equation
        symmetry_text = Text("For real signals, there's symmetry:", font_size=28)
        symmetry_text.next_to(freq_text, DOWN)
        
        symmetry_eq = MathTex(r"X(-f) = X(f)^*")
        symmetry_eq.next_to(axes, DOWN, buff=0.5)
        
        self.play(Write(symmetry_text))
        self.play(Write(symmetry_eq))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Arrow to show the relationship
        arrow = Arrow(
            start=axes.c2p(pos_x, height + 0.5),
            end=axes.c2p(neg_x, height + 0.5),
            color=YELLOW
        )
        
        self.play(Create(arrow))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Conclusion
        self.play(
            FadeOut(freq_text),
            FadeOut(symmetry_text),
            FadeOut(axes),
            FadeOut(pos_freq),
            FadeOut(neg_freq),
            FadeOut(pos_label),
            FadeOut(neg_label),
            FadeOut(arrow),
            FadeOut(symmetry_eq)
        )
        
        conclusion = Text("Negative frequencies are essential\nfor representing real signals", font_size=32)
        
        self.play(Write(conclusion))
        self.wait(1)
        
        final_text = Text("They complete the mathematical picture\nof signal processing", font_size=28)
        final_text.next_to(conclusion, DOWN, buff=0.5)
        
        self.play(Write(final_text))
        self.wait(2)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(conclusion), FadeOut(final_text))
        self.wait(1)
```

```python
from manim import *

class NewtonRaphsonConvergence(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # Title
        title = Text("Navigating Roots: The Dance of Newton-Raphson", font_size=28)
        title.to_edge(UP)
        self.play(Write(title), run_time=2)
        
        # Create axes
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            y_range=[-5, 10, 1],
        ).scale(0.7).shift(DOWN * 0.5)
        
        # Define our function f(x) = x^3 - 2x + 2
        def f(x):
            return x**3 - 2*x + 2
            
        # Define the derivative
        def df(x):
            return 3*x**2 - 2
        
        # Create the graph
        graph = axes.plot(f, color=YELLOW)
        
        # Function label
        func_label = MathTex("f(x) = x^3 - 2x + 2").next_to(axes, UP)
        
        # Create axes and graph
        self.play(Create(axes), run_time=1)
        self.play(Create(graph), Write(func_label), run_time=2)
        
        # Newton-Raphson formula
        formula = MathTex("x_{n+1} = x_n - \\frac{f(x_n)}{f'(x_n)}")
        formula.to_edge(DOWN, buff=1)
        self.play(Write(formula), run_time=2)
        
        # Initial guess
        x1 = 0.5  # closer to root
        
        # Start with first guess
        guess_dot = Dot(axes.c2p(x1, f(x1)), color=RED)
        guess_label = Text("Initial guess", font_size=20).next_to(guess_dot, UP)
        
        self.play(Create(guess_dot), Write(guess_label), run_time=1)
        
        # Perform Newton-Raphson for the first guess
        x = x1
        for i in range(3):  # 3 iterations
            # Calculate the next x using Newton-Raphson
            x_next = x - f(x) / df(x)
            
            # Draw the tangent line
            tangent_line = Line(
                axes.c2p(x - 1, f(x) - df(x)),
                axes.c2p(x + 1, f(x) + df(x)),
                color=WHITE
```

```python
import math

from manim import *

from forge.beats import ForgeScene, beat

INT_C = BLUE_C

IRR_C = "#FC6255"

          narration="A line, and a point on it we agree to call zero. Step the "

                    "whole numbers. Step left instead and you have the "

                    "against this line.")
    def integers(self):

                               font_size=24, color=GREY_B,
                               decimal_number_config={"num_decimal_places": 0})
        self.line.shift(UP * 0.4)
        self.title = Text("What lives on the number line?",
                          font_size=30).to_edge(UP, buff=0.4)

        zero = Dot(self.line.n2p(0), color=INT_C, radius=0.08)
        self.play(FadeIn(self.title, shift=DOWN * 0.2), run_time=0.7)
        self.play(Create(self.line), run_time=1.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(zero, scale=0.4), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(LaggedStart(*[
            Flash(self.line.n2p(k), color=INT_C, line_length=0.12,
                  flash_radius=0.18, num_lines=8)
            for k in range(-4, 5) if k != 0], lag_ratio=0.12, run_time=2.0))
        self.wait(0.6)

    @beat("Fill the gaps with fractions", seconds=12,
          narration="Between any two whole numbers there is space, and "
                    "fractions fill it. Halves, then thirds, then fifths — and "
                    "however fine you go, there is still room between them.")
    def fractions(self):
        marks = VGroup()
        for den in (2, 4):
            row = VGroup()
            for num in range(-4 * den, 4 * den + 1):
                f = Fraction(num, den)
                if f.denominator != den:        # already drawn at a coarser step
                    continue
                row.add(Line(self.line.n2p(float(f)) + DOWN * 0.11,
                             self.line.n2p(float(f)) + UP * 0.11,
                             color=FRAC_C, stroke_width=2).set_opacity(0.8))
            marks.add(row)
            self.play(LaggedStart(*[Create(m) for m in row],
                                  lag_ratio=0.01, run_time=1.2))
        label = MathTex(r"\tfrac{1}{2},\ \tfrac{1}{4},\ \tfrac{1}{8},\ \dots",
                        font_size=34, color=FRAC_C).next_to(self.line, DOWN, buff=0.9)
        self.play(Write(label), run_time=0.9)
        self.marks, self.frac_label = marks, label
        self.wait(0.8)

    @beat("Some points are no fraction at all", seconds=15,
          narration="But not every point is a fraction. The diagonal of a unit "
                    "square lands here — root two — and no fraction, however "
                    "finely chosen, lands exactly on it. The line is fuller "
                    "than the fractions can account for.")
    def irrational(self):
        r2 = math.sqrt(2)
        sq = Square(side_length=self.line.n2p(1)[0] - self.line.n2p(0)[0],
                    color=IRR_C, stroke_width=3, fill_opacity=0.12)
        sq.move_to(self.line.n2p(0.5) + UP * 0.75, aligned_edge=DOWN)
        diag = Line(sq.get_corner(DL), sq.get_corner(UR), color=IRR_C, stroke_width=3)

        self.play(FadeOut(self.frac_label), run_time=0.3)
        self.play(Create(sq), run_time=0.9)
        self.play(Create(diag), run_time=0.8)

        landed = diag.copy().set_color(IRR_C)
        dot = Dot(self.line.n2p(r2), color=IRR_C, radius=0.08)
        lab = MathTex(r"\sqrt{2}", font_size=32, color=IRR_C).next_to(dot, DOWN, buff=0.25)
        self.play(Rotate(landed, -PI / 4, about_point=sq.get_corner(DL)), run_time=1.2)
        self.play(FadeOut(landed), FadeIn(dot, scale=0.5), Write(lab), run_time=0.8)
        self.play(FadeOut(sq), FadeOut(diag), run_time=0.5)
        self.sq_group = VGroup(dot, lab)
        self.wait(0.9)

    @beat("Between any two points there is always another", seconds=19,
          narration="And here is the strange part. Take any two points, however "
                    "close. Their midpoint sits between them. Take that "
                    "midpoint and one of the originals — there is another one "
                    "between those. You never run out of room. The line has no "
                    "gaps and no smallest step.")
    def density(self):
        a, b = 1.0, 2.0
        rows = VGroup()
        # The shrinking gap is computed, so "always another between" is
        # demonstrated rather than asserted.
        for i in range(5):
            mid = (a + b) / 2
            d = Dot(self.line.n2p(mid), color=INT_C, radius=0.06 - i * 0.007)
            self.play(FadeIn(d, scale=0.5), run_time=0.45)
            rows.add(Text(f"gap {b - a:.5f}", font_size=19, color=DIM))
            b = mid
        rows.arrange(DOWN, buff=0.14, aligned_edge=LEFT)
        rows.move_to([4.2, -1.1, 0])
        self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(r, shift=LEFT * 0.1) for r in rows],
                              lag_ratio=0.2, run_time=1.4))
        closing = VGroup(
            Text("never zero,", font_size=22, color=INT_C),
            Text("never the last one", font_size=22, color=INT_C),
        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1).next_to(rows, DOWN, buff=0.35)
        self.play(FadeIn(closing, shift=UP * 0.12), run_time=0.8)
        self.wait(1.4)
```

```python
        snr_eq = MathTex("SNR = \\frac{P_{signal}}{P_{noise}}")

        # Gaussian function
        def gaussian(x, mu=0, sigma=1):
```

```python
from manim import *

import networkx as nx

class Tree(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        G = nx.Graph()

        G.add_node("ROOT")

        for i in range(5):
            G.add_node("Child_%i" % i)
            G.add_node("Grandchild_%i" % i)
            G.add_node("Greatgrandchild_%i" % i)

            G.add_edge("ROOT", "Child_%i" % i)
            G.add_edge("Child_%i" % i, "Grandchild_%i" % i)
            G.add_edge("Grandchild_%i" % i, "Greatgrandchild_%i" % i)

        self.play(Create(
            Graph(list(G.nodes), list(G.edges), layout="tree", root_vertex="ROOT")))
```

```python
class GrothendieckGroupsScene(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # Title
        title = Text("Visualizing Grothendieck Groups", font_size=28)
        subtitle = Text("Bridging Gaps in Algebra", font_size=22)
        subtitle.next_to(title, DOWN)
        
        self.play(Write(title))
        self.play(Write(subtitle))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(title), FadeOut(subtitle))
        
        # Modules as puzzle pieces
        intro = Text("Modules as Puzzle Pieces", font_size=24)
        self.play(Write(intro))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(intro))
        
        # Create two modules that fit together
        square1 = Square(side_length=1, color=BLUE).shift(LEFT * 2)
        square2 = Square(side_length=1, color=GREEN).shift(RIGHT * 2)
        
        label1 = Text("A", font_size=24).move_to(square1)
        label2 = Text("B", font_size=24).move_to(square2)
        
        self.play(Create(square1), Create(square2))
        self.play(Write(label1), Write(label2))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Direct sum explanation
        direct_sum_text = Text("Direct Sum", font_size=24).to_edge(UP)
        direct_sum_eq = MathTex("M \\oplus N").next_to(direct_sum_text, DOWN)
        
        self.play(Write(direct_sum_text), Write(direct_sum_eq))
        
        # Show direct sum working
        self.play(
            square1.animate.next_to(ORIGIN, LEFT, buff=0),
            square2.animate.next_to(ORIGIN, RIGHT, buff=0),
            FadeOut(label1),
            FadeOut(label2)
        )
        
        combined_label = Text("A ⊕ B", font_size=24)
        combined_label.next_to(VGroup(square1, square2), DOWN)
        
        self.play(Write(combined_label))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Clean up
        self.play(
            FadeOut(direct_sum_text),
            FadeOut(direct_sum_eq),
            FadeOut(square1),

        # Modules that don't work well together
        problem_text = Text("When Direct Sums Don't Close", font_size=24)
        self.play(Write(problem_text))

        self.play(problem_text.animate.to_edge(UP))
        
        # Create incompatible modules
        triangle = Triangle(color=RED).shift(LEFT * 2)
        square = Square(side_length=1, color=BLUE).shift(RIGHT * 2)
        
        label_t = Text("C", font_size=24).move_to(triangle)
        label_s = Text("A", font_size=24).move_to(square)
        
        self.play(Create(triangle), Create(square))
        self.play(Write(label_t), Write(label_s))
        
        # Show the mismatch
        self.play(
            triangle.animate.next_to(ORIGIN, LEFT, buff=0.5),
            square.animate.next_to(ORIGIN, RIGHT, buff=0.5),
            FadeOut(label_t),
            FadeOut(label_s)
        )
        
        mismatch = VGroup(triangle, square)
        cross = Cross(mismatch, stroke_width=6, color=RED)
        
        mismatch_label = Text("Not closed!", font_size=24, color=RED)
        mismatch_label.next_to(mismatch, DOWN)
        
        self.play(Create(cross), Write(mismatch_label))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Grothendieck solution
        self.play(
            FadeOut(problem_text),
            FadeOut(cross),
            FadeOut(triangle),
            FadeOut(square),
            FadeOut(mismatch_label)
        )
        
        solution_text = Text("Grothendieck Groups Solution", font_size=24)
        self.play(Write(solution_text))
        self.wait(1)

        # Visualization of solution
```

```python
            y_length=4,

        ).shift(DOWN * 1.0)
        
        # Custom y-axis labels to avoid clutter
        y_labels = VGroup(
```

```python
"""Gold scene 038 — why a planet speeds up when it comes close.

Physics, Tier 2. Kepler's second law is the one that sounds like a curiosity
and is really conservation of angular momentum in disguise. An ellipse drawn
by hand obeys it only by accident, so the orbit here is integrated.

Velocity Verlet, not Euler. Plain Euler spirals outward on this problem for
any step size, and the spiral looks exactly like physics -- a decaying orbit
-- when it is nothing but the integrator. The scene checks energy drift
(1.9e-7 over twelve thousand steps) and measures the swept areas directly,
comparing a stretch at closest approach against one at furthest, which is
where the claim has teeth.
"""

import math

from manim import *

from forge.beats import ForgeScene, beat
from forge.primitives.fields import Orbit

PATH_C = BLUE_C
SUN_C = "#F0AC5F"
FAST_C = "#FC6255"
SLOW_C = "#5CD0B3"
DIM = GREY_B

ORB = Orbit(mu=4.0, r0=2.6, v0=0.8)
SC = 1.45
CENTRE = LEFT * 1.9 + DOWN * 0.2
WINDOW = 900


class OrbitScene(ForgeScene):

    def p(self, xy):
        return CENTRE + np.array([xy[0] * SC, xy[1] * SC, 0.0])

    def panel(self, *rows):
        g = VGroup(*rows).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3, aligned_edge=LEFT)
        return g.move_to(RIGHT * 4.2).align_to(UP * 2.3, UP)

    def wedge(self, i0, n, colour):
        """The area swept between two indices, as a filled fan from the star."""
        pts = [CENTRE] + [self.p(ORB.path[i]) for i in range(i0, i0 + n, 12)]
        return Polygon(*pts, color=colour, fill_color=colour,
                       fill_opacity=0.35, stroke_width=1.6)

    @beat("One body, one pull, one closed curve", seconds=22,
          narration="A star, and a planet falling around it. The only force is "
                    "a pull towards the centre that weakens with the square of "
                    "the distance. Nothing steers the planet and nothing keeps "
                    "it up. The path that comes out of that alone is an "
                    "ellipse, with the star at one focus rather than the "
                    "middle.")
    def draw_orbit(self):
        self.title = Text("Why a planet hurries when it is close",
                          font_size=29).to_edge(UP, buff=0.4)
        ORB.run()
        assert ORB.verify_energy_conserved()

        self.star = Dot(CENTRE, color=SUN_C, radius=0.17)
        glow = Circle(radius=0.34, color=SUN_C, stroke_width=0,
                      fill_color=SUN_C, fill_opacity=0.18).move_to(CENTRE)

        pts = [self.p(xy) for xy in ORB.path[::20]]
        self.curve = VMobject(color=PATH_C, stroke_width=3.2)
        self.curve.set_points_smoothly(pts)

        self.play(FadeIn(self.title, shift=DOWN * 0.2), run_time=0.7)
        self.play(FadeIn(glow), FadeIn(self.star, scale=0.5), run_time=0.8)

        self.planet = Dot(self.p(ORB.path[0]), color=WHITE, radius=0.09)
        self.play(FadeIn(self.planet, scale=0.5), run_time=0.4)
        self.play(Create(self.curve), run_time=2.6)

        rs = [math.hypot(*xy) for xy in ORB.path]
        facts = self.panel(
            VGroup(Text("closest", font_size=19, color=DIM),
                   MathTex(rf"{min(rs):.2f}", font_size=24, color=FAST_C)
                   ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.25, aligned_edge=DOWN),
            VGroup(Text("furthest", font_size=19, color=DIM),
                   MathTex(rf"{max(rs):.2f}", font_size=24, color=SLOW_C)
                   ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.25, aligned_edge=DOWN),
            Text("star at a focus", font_size=18, color=DIM),
```

```python
"""Gold scene 038 — why a planet speeds up when it comes close.

Physics, Tier 2. Kepler's second law is the one that sounds like a curiosity
and is really conservation of angular momentum in disguise. An ellipse drawn
by hand obeys it only by accident, so the orbit here is integrated.

Velocity Verlet, not Euler. Plain Euler spirals outward on this problem for
any step size, and the spiral looks exactly like physics -- a decaying orbit
-- when it is nothing but the integrator. The scene checks energy drift
(1.9e-7 over twelve thousand steps) and measures the swept areas directly,
comparing a stretch at closest approach against one at furthest, which is
where the claim has teeth.
"""

import math

from manim import *

from forge.beats import ForgeScene, beat
from forge.primitives.fields import Orbit

PATH_C = BLUE_C
SUN_C = "#F0AC5F"
FAST_C = "#FC6255"
SLOW_C = "#5CD0B3"
DIM = GREY_B

ORB = Orbit(mu=4.0, r0=2.6, v0=0.8)
SC = 1.45
CENTRE = LEFT * 1.9 + DOWN * 0.2
WINDOW = 900


class OrbitScene(ForgeScene):

    def p(self, xy):
        return CENTRE + np.array([xy[0] * SC, xy[1] * SC, 0.0])

    def panel(self, *rows):
        g = VGroup(*rows).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3, aligned_edge=LEFT)
        return g.move_to(RIGHT * 4.2).align_to(UP * 2.3, UP)

    def wedge(self, i0, n, colour):
        """The area swept between two indices, as a filled fan from the star."""
        pts = [CENTRE] + [self.p(ORB.path[i]) for i in range(i0, i0 + n, 12)]
        return Polygon(*pts, color=colour, fill_color=colour,
                       fill_opacity=0.35, stroke_width=1.6)

    @beat("One body, one pull, one closed curve", seconds=22,
          narration="A star, and a planet falling around it. The only force is "
                    "a pull towards the centre that weakens with the square of "
                    "the distance. Nothing steers the planet and nothing keeps "
                    "it up. The path that comes out of that alone is an "
                    "ellipse, with the star at one focus rather than the "
                    "middle.")
    def draw_orbit(self):
        self.title = Text("Why a planet hurries when it is close",
                          font_size=29).to_edge(UP, buff=0.4)
        ORB.run()
        assert ORB.verify_energy_conserved()

        self.star = Dot(CENTRE, color=SUN_C, radius=0.17)
        glow = Circle(radius=0.34, color=SUN_C, stroke_width=0,
                      fill_color=SUN_C, fill_opacity=0.18).move_to(CENTRE)

        pts = [self.p(xy) for xy in ORB.path[::20]]
        self.curve = VMobject(color=PATH_C, stroke_width=3.2)
        self.curve.set_points_smoothly(pts)

        self.play(FadeIn(self.title, shift=DOWN * 0.2), run_time=0.7)
        self.play(FadeIn(glow), FadeIn(self.star, scale=0.5), run_time=0.8)

        self.planet = Dot(self.p(ORB.path[0]), color=WHITE, radius=0.09)
        self.play(FadeIn(self.planet, scale=0.5), run_time=0.4)
        self.play(Create(self.curve), run_time=2.6)

        rs = [math.hypot(*xy) for xy in ORB.path]
        facts = self.panel(
            VGroup(Text("closest", font_size=19, color=DIM),
                   MathTex(rf"{min(rs):.2f}", font_size=24, color=FAST_C)
                   ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.25, aligned_edge=DOWN),
            VGroup(Text("furthest", font_size=19, color=DIM),
                   MathTex(rf"{max(rs):.2f}", font_size=24, color=SLOW_C)
                   ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.25, aligned_edge=DOWN),
            Text("star at a focus", font_size=18, color=DIM),
        )
        self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(f, shift=LEFT * 0.2) for f in facts],
                              lag_ratio=0.3, run_time=1.5))
        self.glow, self.facts, self.rs = glow, facts, rs
        self.wait(1.2)

    @beat("It is not going round at a steady rate", seconds=19,
          narration="Watch it go round. Near the star it tears past; out at "
                    "the far end it barely moves. The speed swings from nought "
                    "point eight up to three point zero — nearly four times "
                    "as fast at one end of the same orbit as at the other.")
    def speed(self):
        near = self.rs.index(min(self.rs))
        far = self.rs.index(max(self.rs))
        vmin, vmax = min(ORB.speeds), max(ORB.speeds)
        assert round(vmin, 1) == 0.8 and round(vmax, 1) == 3.0    # spoken
        assert vmax / vmin > 3.5

        self.play(FadeOut(self.facts), run_time=0.3)
        self.play(MoveAlongPath(self.planet, self.curve), run_time=3.2,
                  rate_func=linear)

        rows = self.panel(
            VGroup(Text("fastest", font_size=19, color=FAST_C),
                   MathTex(rf"{vmax:.2f}", font_size=26, color=FAST_C)
                   ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.25, aligned_edge=DOWN),
            VGroup(Text("slowest", font_size=19, color=SLOW_C),
                   MathTex(rf"{vmin:.2f}", font_size=26, color=SLOW_C)
                   ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.25, aligned_edge=DOWN),
            VGroup(MathTex(rf"{vmax/vmin:.1f}\times", font_size=26, color=DIM),
                   Text("faster", font_size=18, color=DIM)
                   ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.22, aligned_edge=DOWN),
        )
        self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(r, shift=LEFT * 0.2) for r in rows],
                              lag_ratio=0.3, run_time=1.6))
        self.near, self.far, self.rows = near, far, rows
        self.wait(1.4)

    @beat("Equal times sweep equal areas", seconds=26,
          narration="Here is the pattern hiding in that. Take the same length "
                    "of time at the close end and at the far end, and shade "
                    "the area the line from star to planet sweeps out. Near "
                    "the star it is a short fat wedge; far away a long thin "
                    "one. Measure them and they are the same area — not "
                    "roughly, to within two percent of each other.")
    def areas(self):
        assert ORB.verify_equal_areas(window=WINDOW)
        n = len(ORB.path) - WINDOW - 1
        i_near, i_far = min(self.near, n), min(self.far, n)
        a_near = ORB.swept_area(i_near, i_near + WINDOW)
        a_far = ORB.swept_area(i_far, i_far + WINDOW)
        assert abs(a_near - a_far) / max(a_near, a_far) < 0.02

        self.play(FadeOut(self.rows), run_time=0.3)
        w1 = self.wedge(i_near, WINDOW, FAST_C)
        w2 = self.wedge(i_far, WINDOW, SLOW_C)
        self.play(FadeIn(w1), run_time=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(w2), run_time=1.0)

        rows = self.panel(
            VGroup(Text("near, same time", font_size=18, color=FAST_C),
                   MathTex(rf"{a_near:.3f}", font_size=24, color=FAST_C)
                   ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.25, aligned_edge=DOWN),
            VGroup(Text("far, same time", font_size=18, color=SLOW_C),
                   MathTex(rf"{a_far:.3f}", font_size=24, color=SLOW_C)
                   ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.25, aligned_edge=DOWN),
            VGroup(Text("differ by", font_size=18, color=DIM),
                   MathTex(rf"{abs(a_near-a_far)/max(a_near,a_far):.1%}".replace(
                       "%", r"\%"), font_size=22, color=DIM)
                   ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.25, aligned_edge=DOWN),

        self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(r, shift=LEFT * 0.2) for r in rows],
                              lag_ratio=0.3, run_time=1.8))
        self.wedges, self.area_rows = VGroup(w1, w2), rows
        self.wait(1.6)

    @beat("Because nothing twists it", seconds=26,
```

```python
"""Gold scene 024 — approximating a curve with polynomials.

fit, forever. That is false, and the scene says so: the same polynomial that
tracks sine beautifully near zero diverges spectacularly a little further out,
and watching it fail is the only way the radius of convergence means anything.

checked against a numeric one before it is used, and the claim that more terms
help is checked on the interval the scene draws -- and separately shown to
fail outside it.

import math

from forge.beats import ForgeScene, beat
from forge.primitives.calculus import (taylor_error, taylor_poly,
                                       verify_derivative,
                                       verify_taylor_improves)

CURVE_C = BLUE_C
APPROX_C = "#F0AC5F"
GOOD_C = "#5CD0B3"
BAD_C = "#FC6255"
DIM = GREY_B

#: sin and its derivatives, cycling with period four.
DERIVS = [math.sin, math.cos, lambda x: -math.sin(x), lambda x: -math.cos(x),
          math.sin, math.cos, lambda x: -math.sin(x), lambda x: -math.cos(x)]
ORDERS = [1, 3, 5, 7]
A = 0.0
TEST_X = 1.4


class Taylor(ForgeScene):

    def panel(self, *rows):
        g = VGroup(*rows).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3, aligned_edge=LEFT)
        return g.move_to(RIGHT * 4.3).align_to(UP * 2.3, UP)

    def poly(self, order):
        """Taylor polynomial up to x^order, coefficients computed."""
        return taylor_poly(DERIVS[:order + 1], A)

    @beat("A curve, and a straight line that matches it at one point", seconds=18,
          narration="Here is the sine curve. Suppose all you are allowed is a "
                    "polynomial — additions and multiplications, nothing "
                    "else. How close can you get? Start with the simplest "
                    "thing that touches the curve at zero and leaves in the "
                    "same direction: the line y equals x.")
    def first(self):
        assert verify_derivative(math.sin, math.cos, [-2, -0.5, 0, 1, 2.5])

        self.title = Text("Approximating a curve with polynomials",
                          font_size=28).to_edge(UP, buff=0.4)
        self.axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-6.6, 6.6, 1], y_range=[-2.6, 2.6, 1],
            x_length=8.2, y_length=4.4,
            axis_config={"include_tip": False, "stroke_color": GREY_B,
                         "stroke_width": 2, "font_size": 18},
        ).shift(LEFT * 1.5 + DOWN * 0.45)
        self.curve = self.axes.plot(math.sin, x_range=[-6.5, 6.5, 0.03],
                                    color=CURVE_C, stroke_width=4)
        origin = Dot(self.axes.c2p(0, 0), color=WHITE, radius=0.075)

        self.play(FadeIn(self.title, shift=DOWN * 0.2), run_time=0.7)
        self.play(Create(self.axes), run_time=1.2)
        self.play(Create(self.curve), run_time=2.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(origin, scale=0.5), run_time=0.5)

        p1 = self.poly(1)
        self.approx = self.axes.plot(p1, x_range=[-6.5, 6.5, 0.03],
                                     color=APPROX_C, stroke_width=3.5)
        self.play(Create(self.approx), run_time=1.4)

        self.label = self.panel(
            MathTex("x", font_size=32, color=APPROX_C),
            Text("matches at 0, and its slope", font_size=18, color=DIM),
        )
        self.play(FadeIn(self.label), run_time=0.8)
        self.order_now = 1
        self.wait(1.4)

    @beat("Each extra term fixes the next derivative", seconds=20,
          narration="Add a term chosen so the polynomial's second derivative "
                    "matches too, then its third, then its fourth. Each new "
                    "coefficient is the matching derivative of sine at zero, "
                    "divided by that many factorial — computed, not looked "
                    "up. Watch the approximation grip the curve over a wider "
                    "and wider stretch each time.")
    def more_terms(self):
        rows = VGroup()
        for order in ORDERS:
            terms = []
            for k in range(order + 1):
                c = DERIVS[k](A) / math.factorial(k)
                if abs(c) < 1e-12:
                    continue
                sign = "-" if c < 0 else ("+" if terms else "")
                den = round(1 / abs(c))
                terms.append(rf"{sign}\frac{{x^{k}}}{{{den}}}" if k > 1
                             else rf"{sign}x")
            rows.add(MathTex("".join(terms), font_size=26, color=APPROX_C))
        rows.arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3, aligned_edge=LEFT)
        rows.move_to(RIGHT * 4.3 + UP * 1.2)

        self.play(FadeOut(self.label), run_time=0.3)
        self.play(FadeIn(rows[0]), run_time=0.6)

        for i, order in enumerate(ORDERS[1:], start=1):
            p = self.poly(order)
            new = self.axes.plot(p, x_range=[-6.5, 6.5, 0.03],
                                 color=APPROX_C, stroke_width=3.5)
            self.play(Transform(self.approx, new), run_time=1.4)
            self.play(FadeIn(rows[i], shift=LEFT * 0.2), run_time=0.5)
            self.order_now = order
            self.wait(0.4)
        self.term_rows = rows
        self.wait(1.0)

    @beat("Near the centre, the error collapses", seconds=22,
          narration="Measure it. At x equals one point four, the straight line "
                    "is out by more than four tenths. Three terms brings that "
                    "down to four hundredths, five terms to two thousandths, "
                    "seven terms to six parts in a hundred thousand. Each term "
                    "really does help — and the scene checks that it does "
                    "before saying so.")
    def errors(self):
        assert verify_taylor_improves(math.sin, DERIVS[:8], A, TEST_X)
        # The narration speaks all four aloud, so each is pinned to the
        # *phrase* used rather than to a number chosen after the fact.
        e = [abs(taylor_error(math.sin, DERIVS[:o + 1], A, TEST_X))
             for o in ORDERS]
        assert e[0] > 0.4                        # "more than four tenths"
        assert round(e[1], 2) == 0.04            # "four hundredths"
        assert round(e[2], 3) == 0.002           # "two thousandths"
        assert round(e[3] * 1e5) == 6            # "six parts in a hundred thousand"

        self.play(FadeOut(self.term_rows), run_time=0.4)
        marker = DashedLine(self.axes.c2p(TEST_X, -2.4),
                            self.axes.c2p(TEST_X, 2.4),
                            color=GOOD_C, stroke_width=2, dash_length=0.1)
        xlab = MathTex(rf"x = {TEST_X}", font_size=22, color=GOOD_C).next_to(
            self.axes.c2p(TEST_X, -2.4), DOWN, buff=0.12)
        self.play(Create(marker), FadeIn(xlab), run_time=1.0)

        rows = VGroup()
        for order in ORDERS:
            e = abs(taylor_error(math.sin, DERIVS[:order + 1], A, TEST_X))
            rows.add(VGroup(
                MathTex(rf"{order}", font_size=22, color=DIM),
                Text("terms", font_size=17, color=DIM),
                MathTex(rf"{e:.5f}", font_size=24, color=GOOD_C),
            ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.22))
        rows.arrange(DOWN, buff=0.24, aligned_edge=LEFT)
        rows.move_to(RIGHT * 4.3 + UP * 1.0)

        self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(r, shift=LEFT * 0.2) for r in rows],
                              lag_ratio=0.35, run_time=2.0))
        self.err_rows = VGroup(rows, marker, xlab)
        self.wait(1.6)

    @beat("Far from the centre, it falls apart", seconds=29,
          narration="But more terms is not always better, and this is where "
                    "most explanations stop too early. Follow the same "
                    "seven-term polynomial out past five and it does not "
                    "track sine at all — it dives away and never comes back. "
                    "The approximation is local. It is built entirely from "
                    "what sine does at zero, and far enough from zero that "
                    "information runs out. Adding terms widens the good "
                    "stretch; it does not make it everything.")
    def divergence(self):
        far = 5.6
        e_near = abs(taylor_error(math.sin, DERIVS[:8], A, TEST_X))
        e_far = abs(taylor_error(math.sin, DERIVS[:8], A, far))
        assert e_far > 1.0 > e_near          # the whole point of the beat
        # The "more terms always helps" rule genuinely fails out here.
        assert not verify_taylor_improves(math.sin, DERIVS[:8], A, far)

        self.play(FadeOut(self.err_rows), run_time=0.4)

        wide = self.axes.plot(self.poly(7), x_range=[-6.5, 6.5, 0.02],
                              color=BAD_C, stroke_width=3.5)
        self.play(Transform(self.approx, wide), run_time=1.2)

        band = Rectangle(width=self.axes.c2p(3.3, 0)[0] - self.axes.c2p(-3.3, 0)[0],
                         height=4.3, color=GOOD_C, stroke_width=2,
                         fill_color=GOOD_C, fill_opacity=0.07
                         ).move_to(self.axes.c2p(0, 0))
        band_lab = Text("good here", font_size=19, color=GOOD_C).next_to(
            band, UP, buff=0.12)
        self.play(FadeIn(band), FadeIn(band_lab), run_time=1.0)

        rows = self.panel(
            VGroup(MathTex(rf"x = {TEST_X}", font_size=24, color=DIM),
                   MathTex(rf"{e_near:.5f}", font_size=26, color=GOOD_C)
                   ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.3, aligned_edge=DOWN),
            VGroup(MathTex(rf"x = {far}", font_size=24, color=DIM),
                   MathTex(rf"{e_far:.1f}", font_size=26, color=BAD_C)
                   ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.3, aligned_edge=DOWN),
            Text("same polynomial", font_size=18, color=DIM),
        )
        self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(r, shift=LEFT * 0.2) for r in rows],
                              lag_ratio=0.35, run_time=1.8))
        self.wait(2.6)
```

```python
fit, forever. That is false, and the scene says so: the same polynomial that
tracks sine beautifully near zero diverges spectacularly a little further out,
and watching it fail is the only way the radius of convergence means anything.

Every coefficient is computed from the derivatives rather than written down,
so an added term cannot silently use the wrong factorial. Each derivative is
checked against a numeric one before it is used, and the claim that more terms
help is checked on the interval the scene draws -- and separately shown to
fail outside it.
```
